properties.notes: Creekside industrial and railroad district: soap works with kettles, coal yards, a feed mill, a machine shop with cupola, and stone crushers. There are almost no dwellings. Wewatta's alignment changes south of the viaduct.
Wholesale and foundry district between Wewatta and Wazee. McFarlane & Co. Foundry (cupolas, boiler shop) and a cut-stone works under the 14th St viaduct. There are no dwellings.
Lower downtown manufacturing near Cherry Creek: brass works, machine shops, iron and wire works, and the Western Foundry in Auraria-side 241, which stands right beside tenement rows.
Old Larimer/Market core at Cherry Creek: lodging houses mixed with shops. Two foundries (Central Foundry and the Denver Brass Works) stand south of 14th next to small dwellings.
Edge of the downtown business district: printing, lithography, coffee and candy plants, carriage works. The blocks toward 13th are still mostly dwellings.
Business district fading into a residential zone. Light industry (printing, watch cases, iron beds) sits north of 14th. South of 14th the blocks are almost wholly dwellings.

Uptown edge, mostly residential. The industry here is small: a sausage factory, coffee grinding, an ice cream factory and an instrument factory set among rows of dwellings. Temple Court has its own engine and dynamo plant.
Mostly residential. The trades (tin shop, stone cutting, cigar factory, paints) are on 15th and Glenarm, and the blocks toward 13th are almost all dwellings.
Residential and lodging district near Colfax, with a few small workshops (auto repair, rug factory, Gallup Floral hot houses) mixed into blocks of dwellings.

Old Auraria/West Denver commercial core: Larimer storefronts with small workshops (cigar, bakeries, laundries, blacksmiths, tin shops) and a 40 h.p. bottling works and steam cigar-box factory interspersed with dwellings, tenements, a school and churches.

Cherry Creek splits sheet; East Denver block 101 has a planing mill (shavings fuel, dry kiln) and paint factory with 6 mixers amid dwellings; West Denver block 245 has a marble works, steam bakery and coal yard facing a solid dwelling block across 12th.
Largely residential East Denver blocks along Cherry Creek; industry limited to J.H. Montgomery Machine Co. (30 h.p. engine) on Curtis, Queen City steam laundry (12 h.p.) and small tin/cigar shops.

East Denver residential grid along W. Colfax/Cherry Creek. Notable: J.C. Millen Mfg. Co. chemists occupying floors 1, 6, 7 of an Industrial Bldg with tenements on floors 2-5; Capital Electric lamp works and candy/jelly/bottling shops in block 166.

Heaviest industry so far: Denver Gas & Electric coal-gas plant (retort house, two iron gasometers incl. one-million-gallon, underground coal-tar tanks) plus an ammonia chemical works, facing squatters' shanties and a tar paper factory (pitch kiln, tar tanks) across Wewatta in Grant/West Denver blocks 70-71.

Hungarian Mill & Elevator Co. (400 h.p., 500,000 bu. elevator) and Anheuser Busch beer depot sit amid dense Grant/West Denver dwelling blocks along Wazee and W. Walnut; D&RG yard occupies the Wynkoop side.

Most industrial of the batch's residential sheets: Tivoli Union Brewing (125' stack, ice machine), E.M. Davis Iron Works foundry and machine shops, Excelsior flour mill, glass works and brass foundry, all sharing blocks with dwellings, hotels and halls in Grant/West Denver (Auraria).
Mixed: dwellings on 6th-7th face stone yards and a marble works; Kindel mattress factory (fire-prone picker rooms) shares block with ~11 dwellings. Rail yards both sides.

Heavily industrial lower downtown along D&RG tracks: Western Boiler Works, Hallack & Howard lumber, Ayres feed mill, an idle ore sampling works, junk yard. Only block 257 has a real dwelling cluster (~12).

Major hazard: Denver Gas & Electric Co. electric light plant (several thousand h.p., 150 ft stack) sharing block 104 with ~17 dwellings. Planing mill and box factory share block 102 with ~17 dwellings and a boarding house.
Eagle Mill & Elevator flour mill (water power) in block with ~16 dwellings; lumber yard behind a dwelling row. Most of lower sheet blank (beyond mapped area).
Queen City Foundry (cupolas) and Capitol Ice houses face a 22-dwelling block across 3rd; Bingham lumber yard faces dwellings across W. Walnut. Planing-mill name in block 269 is uncertain.
Mostly residential near W. Colfax with C&S tracks to the north; the Chamberlain-Dillingham ore sampling mill shares block 268 with a row of dwellings.

West edge of Auraria on the South Platte: vacant Jerome's Broadway lots and a row of 11 cottages in Overland Park west of S. Broadway; Baker's/Villa Sub. mixes congregations, a school and dwellings with blacksmiths, a soap factory/shoddy mill, the Lacombe Electric power plant, a lard renderer and the D.L.&G. roundhouse.

Rail corridor through Baker's Sub.: Colorado Ice & Storage plant (300 tons/day) and the cement-products factory in the old tramway power house sit by the tracks on W. Colfax; everything south of W. 14th is vacant platted lots.
Mostly vacant Fletcher's West Side and Milleson's lots between S. 2nd and the C.&S. R.R.; McGargee & Mallen pickle works (with a second plant in the old mica mill) beside a handful of dwellings.

Edge-of-city sheet near W. Alameda and S. Santa Fe: one residential block (Norwood Add'n block 5) faces a lumber yard and coal yard along rail lines, with the Colorado Zinc Co. ore separator mill in open ground to the south. Two streets are labelled W. Alameda Av (one at the top and one diagonal along the section line), so the crossing coordinates for the diagonal one are approximate.

Lower downtown rail district from 15th to 17th St: freight depots, the Union Depot yards, a hides, wool and tallow warehouse, the Wilfley concentrator machine shop, the Paulson fixture planing mill and a Coors beer and ice warehouse. The only housing is three dwellings and two hotels in block 10.

Rail and utility district around 17th-19th Sts: a Pintsch gas plant, the Denver City Steam Heat boiler plant (140 ft stack) and the Denver Iron Works foundry. Four dwellings and three hotels or boarding houses in block D share the block with the foundry and face the gas plant across Wewatta.

Wholesale warehouse district on Wynkoop and Wazee between 15th and 17th: grocery houses, implement and hardware warehouses, a candy factory and a coffee and spice mill. No dwellings; the only lodging is the Hotel Oxford.

Dense lower-downtown wholesale blocks between Wazee and Blake: food processing (coffee mill, candy, sausage), a type foundry, steam laundry, liveries and blacksmiths beside hotels. The only dwellings are six units in the 'Chinese Quarters' inside block 20.

Wholesale and light-industry blocks between Blake and Market, 15th-17th: a brass foundry and plating works (Creswell) that powers neighbouring shops, the Colorado Lead Works, candy and cigar factories, creamery and laundries beside hotels. No dwellings.

Market Street commission-house row and Larimer Street commercial front, 15th-17th Sts: produce and wholesale warehouses, cheap lodging houses and small shops. The only power plant is the basement electric light plant in the Railroad Bldg. No dwellings.

Larimer-Lawrence retail core, 15th-17th: stores, saloons and lodging hotels, with small trades (printing, bindery, tent and awning) and basement dynamo plants in the department stores. No dwellings and no heavy industry.

Downtown 16th St. between Stout and California; commercial with large basement power plants, light manufacturing on upper floors (furniture, mattress), Chinese laundry and tin shop; essentially no housing.

16th St. between California and Welton, at the edge of the core: still mainly commercial but with a few dwellings behind stores and a denser cluster of small shops (blacksmith, tin/sheet iron, dyeing, patent medicine, assay furnace).
16th St. between Welton and Glenarm, the eastern fringe of downtown where stores give way to houses. Dwellings sit beside a furniture factory, jewelry works and alley warehouses; no heavy industry.

Edge of downtown between Glenarm and Court Pl.: detached houses share blocks with carpenter shops, tin/novelty/plumbing shops, a trunk factory, auto garage, printing and Chinese laundries; small-scale but intimate mixing. Broadway/17th Av crossing at upper right, not recorded as coordinates uncertain.

Court Pl./Cleveland Pl./Broadway near 16th and Colfax, a mixed fringe of stores, lodgings and small frame houses intermingled with auto garages, machine shops, laundries, a blacksmith and the big Omnibus & Cab Co. stable. Inset shows the London Dairy, 6 miles NE.

Lower downtown rail district along Wynkoop/Wazee, 17th-19th: warehouses, the McPhee & McGinnity planing mill (shavings-fired boilers) and lumber yard, an idle iron works and an ore-car maker. Very little housing; a hotel and a lone dwelling sit next to the mill block.

Downtown 16th St. between Lawrence and Arapahoe, wholly commercial with lodgings above stores and no dwellings. Industry is light but includes a packing-house ice/sausage/lard-rendering plant in a basement, printing plants and basement boiler/dynamo plants.

Downtown 16th St. between Arapahoe and Curtis; commercial/civic only, no dwellings. Industry limited to Denver Post and job printing with electrotype foundries, a shirt factory and basement power plants.
Downtown 16th St. between Curtis and Champa; fully commercial, no dwellings. Only light trades: candy/ice-cream, printing, shirt/shirtwaist factories, furniture repairing, bicycle shop.

Downtown 16th St. between Champa and Stout; commercial, no dwellings. Block 130's alley holds the densest cluster of workshops on these sheets (blacksmith/machine, wire & iron works, tin, paint, cabinet, shoe and candy shops).

Wazee-Blake, 17th-19th, Congressional Grant East Denver: dense machine-shop/foundry district (Vulcan Iron Works, Enz & Orr, Buchanan) plus lumber yard; essentially no housing. Engine House No. 5 on Blake.

Blake-Market, 17th-19th: food processing (National Biscuit, Continental Biscuit, candy) next to lead foundry, paint mill, planing mills, lard rendering and Capital Ice plant; only lodging/hotel housing.

Market-Larimer, 17th-19th: hotel/lodging-house and saloon district (Windsor Hotel, Barclay Block) with small factories (overalls, sausage & lard rendering, creamery, glove, harness). No single-family dwellings.
Larimer-Lawrence, 17th-19th: skid-row commercial strip (2nd-hand, saloons) with small workshops, an ore mill, assay furnaces, steam dye works; a handful of alley dwellings.
Lawrence-Arapahoe, 17th-19th: downtown mixed commercial; stables, ore mill and several assay furnaces, printing, dyeing; few dwellings (5) plus two hotels.
Arapahoe-Curtis, 17th-19th: transition edge; Curtis side of block 95 still single-family houses facing a steam laundry/livery across the alley; assay lab, harness factory and Empire Theatre to south.
Curtis-Champa, 17th-19th: northern block still largely single-family (18 D) interleaved with printing plants and small shops; southern block commercial with theatre and Doss Bros. plating works.
Champa-Stout, 17th-19th: small-shop downtown fringe; 10 dwellings mostly on Stout amid assay furnaces, electrotype foundry, stamping and motor works.

Stout-California, 17th-19th: apartments/hotels and ~16 detached dwellings on California and Stout interleaved with printing plants (Smith Brooks electrotype foundry), an ore mill in a basement, bakery and hotel power plant.
California-Welton, 17th-19th: predominantly residential (29 D) with tin & sheet iron works, assay furnaces/ore mill, stable annex and Chinese laundries tucked among houses.

Downtown Welton-Tremont, 17th-18th: commercial with scattered dwellings, small workshops (sawing, carpet cleaning, printing, plumbing). Upper right holds insets of an isolated tallow/rendering works and a gold extraction works along the South Platte.

Railroad-side residential area at Delgany/New Haven 19th-21st, wedged between B.&M.R.R. tracks and a large Rocky Mountain Fuel Co. coal yard; small workshops (stables, stone yards, bakery) mixed with cottages. 'Old Buildings' lane name uncertain.
Rail-yard edge: two working-class residential blocks west of Wewatta, stone yards and warehouses between Wewatta and Wynkoop, and the U.P. freight yard east to Wazee.

Lower downtown Wazee-Market, 19th-21st: warehouses, gas holder, carpet and sausage works on rail spurs west of Blake; Market St. red-light/Chinese quarter east of it, with cottages wedged between. Sanborn blocks 1 and 24 are two halves of one Wazee-Blake city block.

Larimer St. commercial strip with Market St. red-light district (dozens of F.B. houses) on the west and cottages along Lawrence on the east; industry is small-scale (laundries, bakeries, tin/plumbing shops, livery).

Residential Lawrence-Curtis blocks 19th-21st, heavily interspersed with small workshops (carpenters, bakeries, blacksmith/wagon painting, machine shop with lodgings above, furnace and stove shops, cigar factory).
Residential Curtis-Stout blocks 19th-21st with Engine Ho. No. 4; small workshops cluster on Curtis and Champa (liveries, assay office, machine shop, cigar factory, laundries, bakery).
Almost entirely residential Stout-Welton blocks 19th-21st with East Denver High School; only notable workshop is the Electric Flash Light Co. machine shop among cottages.

Upper/left: residential Clements' Add. blocks between Welton and Grant around Broadway/20th Av. Lower right, separated by a heavy line, is an inset of the Standard Meat and Livestock Co. packing plant and stock yards 6 miles NE of the P.O. on Sand Creek, with slaughter, tallow/fertilizer tanks and about 6 dwellings on the grounds; coordinates in that inset are not on the city grid.

Shanty settlement on disputed South Platte river-bottom ground west of the B&M tracks; Crescent flour mill/elevator and Hendrie & Bolthoff warehouses along Corbett, with shanties and dwellings in the same block.

Gaston's Add'n beside the U.P. yard: Sayre Newton lumber/planing mill, Halleck paint & varnish works, Kuner pickle-vinegar works and steam laundry interleaved with dwellings and Market St 'F.B.' houses.
Mixed commercial-residential blocks of the 2100-2200 range (Market to Arapahoe): Market St F.B. houses, liveries, Chinese laundries, small machine shops and carriage works among dwellings.
Residential blocks between Arapahoe and Champa near 22nd St with corner stores; small trades only (Chinese laundry, furniture repair, bakery, printing, a livery), plus East Denver Turn Hall.
Almost wholly residential (dwellings, flats, apartments, churches) between Stout and Welton; industry limited to laundries, a bakery, upholstery, paint/oil shop and a blacksmith.
Fully residential area of row houses, flats and churches between Welton and Logan; only a bicycle shop, hand laundries, a bakery and a feed & coal store.
Union Pacific yard with roundhouse/repair shop and two large lumber yards along Blake at 26th-27th; essentially no housing.

Mostly Union Pacific rail yard; east edge has lumber yards, steel & wire warehouse and one mixed block (23rd-24th, Blake) where ~13 dwellings sit beside a lumber yard and express stable. 23rd St viaduct marked closed.

Dense mixed working-class blocks around 25th-27th between Blake and Lawrence. Furniture/bed factory, paint factory and lumber yard share a block with shanties and dwellings below grade; workshops (coppersmith, tin shop, bakeries) dispersed among houses.

Six mixed blocks 23rd-25th, Blake to Lawrence. Two steam laundries with boilers, a wagon & carriage works with blacksmith and paint shop, and many small shops interleaved with dwellings and tenements; schools on Walnut.
Almost purely residential sheet (Lawrence to Champa, 25th-27th): row houses and detached dwellings, one bakery with oven, a church and the State Armory drill room. Comparison-group area.
Mostly residential (Lawrence to Champa, 23rd-25th) with a few workshops: cigar-box factory and carriage works on Lawrence, D&RG express stables on Arapahoe; synagogue and church on Curtis.
Residential sheet (Champa to Welton, 23rd-25th) with row houses, boarding houses, churches; only a carpenter shop as industry. Block 154 entirely vacant.
Entirely residential (Champa to east of California, 25th-27th); no industrial or workshop uses. Good comparison area.

West half residential with a commercial node at 27th & Welton (artesian-water bottling with gasoline engine, bakery, tin shop). East of Washington Av. (detail in Volume 3) lies the UP rail corridor with a building-supply mill with boilers, scrap iron yard and abandoned ore mill, scattered dwellings along 31st.

27th-29th, UP yard to Larimer. An ore sampling works (crusher, furnace, 40 h.p. engine, 45 ft chimney) and big lumber yard on Blake face a block of ~48 dwellings; asbestos covering factory set among row houses. Bake houses and stores line Larimer.

Five Points area, Larimer-Curtis between 27th and 29th: predominantly dwellings with Larimer St commercial strip. Main hazard City Steam Laundry with boilers and 35 h.p. engine amid dwellings on Lawrence. Map orientation taken as top=N (29th) and left=W (Larimer).
Fully residential Five Points blocks (Curtis-California, 27th-29th) with a few corner stores and one bakery; no significant industry. Top taken as N (29th), left as W (Curtis).

Residential Five Points blocks California-Grant, 26th-29th, with small shops; notable is an oleomargarine factory with render kettle and gasoline engine attached to a dwelling at Lincoln Av & Emerson St. Top taken as N.

Blake-Larimer, 29th-31st beside the Union Pacific yards. Major hazard: Denver Engineering Works foundry/boiler/machine shops (cupolas, core ovens, 60 h.p. engine) next to the St. Nicholas Hotel and across Blake from dwellings; two steam laundries and the Weigele steel pipe works also amid housing.

Larimer-Curtis, 29th-31st: residential blocks with vacant lots; Larimer strip has a carriage & wagon works (blacksmith, paint shop) and Denver Balance Co. instrument shop with gas engine. Top taken as N.
Sparsely built residential blocks Curtis-California, 29th-31st, with many vacant lots; no industry. Gilpin School occupies half of block 67. Top taken as N.

Residential Five Points blocks (California-Lincoln, 29th-31st) plus an inset of St. Vincent's Add'n (Wewatta/Wynkoop at 43rd, mostly unplotted). Grant Smelter ground is referenced to sheet 261 but not drawn here; only a livery and small shops on this sheet.
Purely residential blocks east of Downing (Downing-Humboldt, 26th-28th) with a small bake house; no industry. North is up on this sheet.
Residential blocks Humboldt-Williams, 26th-28th Av.; only industrial-type use is the Manual Training High School shops (machine shop, blacksmith, 50 h.p. engines, dynamos, boilers). North up.
Residential blocks Downing-Humboldt, 28th-30th Av., with many vacant lots; only a livery stable and small storage rooms; no industry. North up.

Purely residential Whittier-area blocks (Downing's/McMann's Add'ns) with frame and brick dwellings and stables; only a tiny warehouse behind corner stores at 30th & Franklin. Fuller Park occupies the SE block.
Residential only, western half built up with frame/brick dwellings and attached rows; Race-Vine and the eastern half-blocks are entirely vacant platted lots. No industry.
Residential edge of development: Williams-High blocks built up with dwellings and attached rows, everything east of High vacant platted lots. No industry. Area south of 26th Av. is in Volume Three.

Mixed industrial-residential Curtis Park/Five Points edge beside the Union Pacific: Denver City Tramway Blake St. power house with open coal piles and Denver Fire Clay Co. kiln works (secret process) directly across Blake from dense worker rows; blacksmith, feed stable and marble shop interspersed.

Residential Curtis Park neighbourhood; industry confined to Larimer frontage (Metropolitan and Atlas steam laundries, Chinese laundry, blacksmith) and the small American Cleaning & Dyeing Wks behind Curtis St. dwellings.
Dense Five Points/Curtis Park residential sheet; industry limited to McClear's small machine shop on Stout, a broom factory on an alley, and a meat smokehouse, all embedded among dwellings.
Solidly residential Whittier blocks with two churches and a small commercial strip on Downing; only a coal & feed yard and a rear bake house.
Residential Whittier blocks with a church, a small drug-store/barber cluster at 31st & Gilpin; only industry is the Vienna Model Bakery oven tucked behind Franklin St. dwellings.

Two-panel sheet of purely residential Whittier/Cole blocks (east of Williams/High): regular frame cottages and attached rows, much vacant land east of High; no industry. Duplicate block numbers between panels marked with 'b'.

Ironton/Cole area east of the rail yards: worker dwellings on Delgany-Wewatta-Wynkoop blocks within one block of the Star Boiler & Sheet Iron Wks and the J. Geo. Leyner air-compressor/rock-drill works on Wazee; Wynkoop-Wazee blocks otherwise vacant.

Ironton Addition, north Denver along the Union Pacific: the large Colorado Iron Works foundry fills the block south of 34th, Denver Boiler & Sheet Iron Wks and Atlas coal yard lie one street from rows of dwellings on Wewatta/Wynkoop. Asphalt mill with rotary driers by the UP tracks.

Mixed working-class district at Blake/Walnut/Downing near 36th-38th: Burkhardt slaughterhouse and stockyard directly across Downing Av. from a dense row of stores and dwellings; Rauh Marble Works, coal/feed yards, blacksmiths, carriage works and a cigar factory interleaved with housing.

Dense working-class blocks (Blake/Walnut/Larimer, 33rd-35th) with many attached rows; industry is small-scale and embedded: cracker factory, bakehouse, bottling works, three blacksmiths, a paint shop and coal yards, with the UP rail yard to the west.

Residential Witter's and Case & Ebert's additions (Larimer to Curtis, 33rd-35th) with few industries: Turner Moving & Storage warehouses, a cornice shop, plumbing and novelty works; two Baptist churches and a hose company/police station.
Hyde Park Add'n (Downing to Humboldt, 34th-36th Avs.): an almost wholly residential comparison area; the only industrial structure is a vacant former planing mill inside block 3.
Residential Curtis Park/Hyde Park edge with much vacant land; only a florist's greenhouse plant, a bakery and a coal/hay/grain dealer; Maria Mitchell School boiler plant.
Entirely residential sheet (Humboldt to Williams, 32nd-34th Avs.) with attached rows and a few corner stores; no industrial establishments: a clean comparison area.

Residential Hyde Park area (Humboldt-Williams, 34th-36th Avs.) whose one large plant is the Denver Tramway car barn (boiler, engine & dynamo, oil room) facing dense attached rows across Gilpin; otherwise a bakery and a carpenter shop.

Two-panel sheet of Hyde Park / Providence Park / Park / Ford's additions (Williams-High, 34th-38th Avs.): residential with attached terraces and large vacant tracts; no industrial plants except an oven outbuilding of uncertain use.

Hyde Park / Riverside additions where the diagonal downtown grid (Downing Av., Larimer, 38th St.) meets the avenue grid; residential with small trades: two bakeries, a paints & oils store, a plumbing shop and a hand laundry.

Purely residential Clayton/Cole-area sheet (Humboldt to Williams, 36th-38th Avs): 1-1.5 story frame and brick dwellings, two churches, Hyde Park School, a few corner stores. No industrial establishments.

Riverside/Ironton near UP yard (Wewatta to Blake, 38th-40th). Worker-housing rows share the Wynkoop-Wazee block with the Union Ore Extraction & Reduction Works (leaching/settling tanks, crusher, furnace) and a sausage factory with rendering kettle.

Edge of Cole/Elyria by the U.P.R.R.: J. R. Parr's planing mill and Hallack Lumber Co. yard fill block 2 between 39th and 40th Avs., facing residential blocks across Franklin and 39th Av. Rest is residential.

Thinly built Park/Hodgson's/Swansea additions (Williams to Vine, 38th-40th Avs). Dwellings, two lodging houses and saloons only; no industry. Woodie (north of 39th) appears to continue as Race south of 39th; modern name not printed.

Almost entirely Union Pacific yard: UP roundhouse/repair shops and Pullman Co. car shops (125 ft stack, boilers, paint shop) just north of 40th Av., with an inset of the National Fuse & Powder Co. fuse factory (powder houses, tar room) at 38th & Delgany. No dwellings on the sheet; residential blocks of sheets 243/244 lie across 40th Av.

Pullman Co. car shops (woodworking, paint and varnish, benzine cleaning) directly north of 40th Av., across from the residential blocks of sheet 244 (High to Vine). Insets: Columbine School block and Railway Steel Spring Co. (naphtha house, 75 ft stack) at 41st Av. & York.

Sparsely built Elyria blocks (Race-Gaylord, 43rd-45th Avs), mostly vacant lots, bounded west by UP/Southern Pacific railroad grounds. Insets: Riverside Cemetery with pump/boiler houses, a granite works and a greenhouse. No heavy industry on this sheet.
Thinly settled Elyria/Swansea blocks (Gaylord-Josephine, 43rd-45th Avs), mostly vacant lots; one church, two saloons. Only industry is T. W. Casey wood & coal yard on the U.P.R.R. (inset).

Dense Elyria worker housing (Cline to Baldwin, Fisk to Western/46th Av.) with saloons and a Western Breeders Ass'n cattle yard inside block 3; south half is St. Vincent's Add'n cut by UP and C&S switches with 'Grant Smelter beyond' noted.

Elyria/Swansea residential area, sparsely built (mostly vacant lots), with a few stores, a bakery oven and a small glove manufactory; Colorado & Eastern R.R. and U.P.R.R. tracks at SW corner. Town hall at Fisk & London.
Thinly built Elyria residential blocks with no industry; U.P.R.R. tracks cross diagonally SW-NE.
Sparse Elyria/Swansea residential blocks with no industrial plants; U.P.R.R. main line cuts diagonally across the NW. Many wholly vacant platted blocks south of Western Av.
Swansea residential sheet with no industry: worker housing rows, Swansea School and Mt. Olivet Baptist Church; many vacant lots.
Swansea residential with a 'Swansea Terrace' flats row; only industry is Anderson Bros coal & wood yard by the U.P.R.R. (inset). Dunham Park NE.
Elyria fringe beside Denver Union Stock Yards and B.& M.R.R.; cattle shed and stockyard platform close to Ward's Hotel and dwellings; Colorado & Eastern coal road runs through block 9.

Elyria residential sheet without industrial plants; Colorado & Eastern R.R. narrow-gauge coal road runs along Frank. 3 Mile House roadhouse/dance hall at Baldwin & Frank. Upper-right quarter (blocks 42-43) judged from overview only; all vacant.
Elyria residential; no industry. Colorado & Eastern R.R. narrow-gauge coal road runs along Frank. Northern blocks (Kenner's Sub.) nearly vacant.
Elyria/Swansea edge: mostly small dwellings and vacant lots; Bradbury contractor's wagon yard beside the U.P.R.R. diagonal; Colorado & Eastern narrow-gauge along Frank.
